channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Kazakhstan's government reshuffled following parliamentary elections
item.description: Following the adoption of a new constitution and the election of a unicameral parliament, Kazakhstan has formed a new political structure. Olzhas Bektenov has been reappointed Prime Minister, Yrlan Karin appointed Vice President, and Aybek Dadebay elected Speaker of the newly formed Kurultai.

item.title: Tajikistan's Emomali Rahmon and Russia's Vladimir Putin discuss security, trade, and energy
item.description: During a meeting in Bishkek on the sidelines of the SCO summit, Tajik President Emomali Rahmon and Russian President Vladimir Putin discussed bilateral cooperation. Key topics included security, stability, trade, economic, and cultural-humanitarian ties, as well as energy and investment cooperation.

item.title: Putin: Russia will withdraw military base from Armenia if requested
item.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin stated that Russia is prepared to withdraw its military base from Gyumri, Armenia, if the Armenian government no longer desires its presence. This statement follows discussions regarding Armenia's potential EU membership and its implications for relations with Russia and the EAEU.

item.title: Putin dismisses rumors of new Russian mobilization as 'nonsense'
item.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin called rumors of a potential new mobilization in Russia 'utter nonsense.' Speaking to journalists in Bishkek after the SCO summit, Putin stated these reports are an 'information attack on Russia.' He also expressed Russia's desire to end the war in Ukraine and achieve lasting peace through negotiations.

item.title: US and Iran exchange strikes amid escalating tensions, civilian and military casualties reported
item.description: Tensions between the US and Iran have escalated with both sides exchanging further strikes. Reports indicate civilian and military casualties resulted from airstrikes, including an attack during a wedding near Sirik coast where a four-year-old child was among the dead. The situation remains tense.

item.title: Putin thanks Japarov for supporting Russian language and cooperation in education
item.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin expressed appreciation for Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov's support of the Russian language, which holds national language status in Kyrgyzstan. Putin noted the joint launch of nine schools with Russian as the language of instruction, expecting the first to open by September 1, 2024.

item.title: Tajikistan and India Discuss Expanding Cooperation in Bishkek
item.description: Tajikistan's President Emomali Rahmon and India's Prime Minister Narendra Modi met in Bishkek on the sidelines of the SCO summit. They discussed expanding practical and trust-based cooperation, focusing on political, economic, scientific, educational, cultural, and security spheres. Both sides emphasized the importance of continued high-level dialogue.

item.title: UN Expert Urges Tajikistan to Diversify Economy and Improve Financial Transparency
item.description: A UN expert, Atiya Waris, visited Tajikistan and emphasized the need to link economic policy with human rights implementation. The expert called for economic diversification and greater financial transparency within the country. Further details were not immediately available.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan: Ruble Nears Som, Euro and Yuan Decline on September 2
item.description: On September 2, the Russian ruble approached the Kyrgyzstani som, reaching a monthly low. The euro, Kazakh tenge, and Chinese yuan also depreciated against the som, while the US dollar remained stable. These currency fluctuations are based on data from the National Bank of Kyrgyzstan and exchange bureaus.

item.title: Kyrgyz President Awards Rosatom Head with Dostuk Order
item.description: Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov awarded the Dostuk Order to Alexey Likhachev, head of the Rosatom state corporation. The award recognizes significant contributions to developing interstate cooperation. The ceremony took place in Bishkek during official talks between the leaders of Kyrgyzstan and Russia.

item.title: Putin Thanks Japarov for Flawless SCO Summit Organization
item.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin expressed gratitude to Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov for the flawless organization of the SCO Summit in Bishkek. Putin stated the summit was held at the highest international level, with significant work accomplished and important documents adopted. He congratulated Japarov and his team on the successful outcome.

item.title: ADB to Fund $400 Million for Central Asia Border Crossing Modernization
item.description: The Asian Development Bank (ADB) has approved $400 million to modernize border crossings in the Central Asia Regional Economic Cooperation (CAREC) region. The BUILD program aims to reduce transport costs, improve goods and people movement, and enhance regional connectivity. This initiative will help make borders faster, smarter, and more interconnected.

item.title: Tajikistan Plans Over 1,100 New Electric Vehicle Charging Stations by 2028
item.description: Tajikistan plans to build 1,100 new electric vehicle charging stations between 2026 and 2028, with over half designated for Dushanbe. The initiative, part of the 'Program for the Development of Electric Transport,' requires over $18 million. The plan also includes expanding the electric bus fleet and establishing specialized maintenance points.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan President Sadyr Japarov and Russian President Vladimir Putin Hold Talks in Bishkek
item.description: Kyrgyzstan President Sadyr Japarov met with Russian President Vladimir Putin in Bishkek to discuss bilateral cooperation, including energy, trade, education, and security. Japarov thanked Russia for agreeing to host the 2028 World Nomad Games. Putin congratulated Kyrgyzstan on its Independence Day and praised Bishkek's organization of the SCO summit.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan and Russia Presidents Discuss Cooperation in Bishkek
item.description: Kyrgyzstan President Sadyr Japarov and Russian President Vladimir Putin held talks in Bishkek, discussing bilateral cooperation in energy, trade, education, and security. Japarov thanked Russia for agreeing to host the 2028 World Nomad Games, with Kyrgyzstan offering support. Putin congratulated Japarov on Independence Day and praised Bishkek's SCO summit preparations.

item.title: Uzbek President Concludes Working Visit to Kyrgyzstan for SCO Summit
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev concluded his working visit to Bishkek, participating in the jubilee session of the SCO Heads of State Council. Key discussions focused on the SCO's 25-year development and future cooperation priorities. Mirziyoyev proposed initiatives on industrial cooperation, transport connectivity, digital technologies, and security, leading to the adoption of the Bishkek Declaration.

item.title: Uzbekistan's First Lady Attends SCO Summit Cultural Events in Bishkek
item.description: Uzbekistan's First Lady, Ziroat Mirziyoyeva, participated in cultural events in Bishkek during the SCO summit. She joined the First Ladies of Kyrgyzstan, Azerbaijan, Turkey, and China. The group viewed an exhibition of Kyrgyz folk art and witnessed demonstrations of traditional hunting with falcons.

item.title: Putin and Pashinyan Discuss Armenia's Potential EU Accession in Bishkek
item.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin and Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan held talks in Bishkek, focusing on Armenia's intention to join the EU. Putin expressed respect for Armenia's choice but noted potential complexities for cooperation within the Eurasian Economic Union. Pashinyan affirmed Armenia's interest in deepening ties with Russia.

item.title: Putin and Pashinyan Discuss Armenia's Potential EU Accession in Bishkek
item.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin and Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan held talks in Bishkek, focusing on Armenia's intention to join the EU and its implications for Russia relations. Putin stated Russia respects Armenia's choice but needs clarity on its future political and economic course. Pashinyan affirmed Armenia's interest in deepening ties with Russia and sees no conflict with EU aspirations.

item.title: Woman Dies in Osh Region Hospital After Allegedly Being Beaten by Husband
item.description: A 37-year-old woman has died in a hospital in the Uzgen district of Osh region, days after allegedly being severely beaten by her husband. A video showing her injuries circulated online. Police opened a criminal case for minor bodily harm due to conflicting testimonies, but are now investigating the cause of death after her passing.

item.title: Uzbekistan and India aim to boost bilateral trade to $5 billion by 2030
item.description: Uzbekistan and India intend to increase mutual trade volume to $5 billion by 2030. Following Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi's state visit, discussions focused on expanding trade, economic ties, digital payment systems, and cooperation in environmental protection, education, science, culture, traditional medicine, mining, and agriculture.

item.title: Indian PM Modi urged Putin to stop war in Ukraine at SCO summit in Bishkek
item.description: During the SCO summit in Bishkek, Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi called on Russian President Vladimir Putin to cease the war against Ukraine. The summit provided a platform for this significant international appeal.

item.title: Uzbek President outlines vision for SCO+ and UN cooperation in a multipolar world
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev addressed the SCO+ meeting on the UN's role in a just world order. He emphasized that regional organizations should complement the UN's central coordinating role by facilitating practical implementation of global principles based on local conditions and needs. The SCO+ format can unite states and organizations around a common agenda.

item.title: Uzbek President outlines vision for SCO+ and UN cooperation in a multipolar world
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev participated in the SCO+ meeting on the UN's role in a just world order. He emphasized that regional organizations should complement the UN's central coordinating role by facilitating practical implementation of global principles based on local conditions and needs. The SCO+ format can unite states and organizations around a common agenda.

item.title: Uzbekistan to halve customs clearance times by 2030
item.description: Uzbekistan aims to reduce customs clearance times to two hours for imports and 30 minutes for exports by 2030. The goal is to simplify customs procedures for entrepreneurs and speed up the movement of goods into and out of the country, with a target of 60% of customs clearance being human-factor-free.

item.title: Putin expresses Russian solidarity with Iran at SCO Summit
item.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin met with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian at the SCO Summit in Bishkek. Putin conveyed the Russian people's solidarity with Iran's pursuit of national interests, sovereignty, and independence. He also sent greetings to Iran's Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei.

item.title: Putin expresses Russian solidarity with Iran at SCO Summit in Bishkek
item.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin met with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian at the SCO Summit. Putin conveyed the Russian people's solidarity with Iran in its pursuit of national interests, sovereignty, and independence. He also sent greetings to Iran's Supreme Leader.

item.title: Tajik President Emomali Rahmon to visit Iran soon
item.description: Tajik President Emomali Rahmon announced he will travel to Iran in the coming months. Discussions were also held with the Indian Prime Minister regarding visa-free travel for tourists between the two countries. Separately, the National Encyclopedia of Tajikistan is organizing a calligraphy course.

item.title: Kyrgyz President Japarov concludes SCO Plus meeting in Bishkek
item.description: Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov announced the conclusion of the SCO Plus meeting in Bishkek. He emphasized the agreement on maintaining dialogue and relying on international law, and the need to strengthen the UN's role in a just, multipolar world. The meeting discussed international security and cooperation.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Parliament Focuses on Social Development and Citizen Interests
item.description: Uzbekistan's parliament is tasked with evaluating laws' impact on citizens, controlling their execution, and incorporating public interests into state policy. This approach aligns with a UN resolution initiated by Uzbekistan, emphasizing parliaments' role in social development. The 150th Inter-Parliamentary Union Assembly was recently held in Tashkent.

item.title: Tajikistan Increases Salaries, Pensions, and Stipends by 15-25% Starting September 1, 2026
item.description: Starting September 1, 2026, salaries and pensions in Tajikistan will increase by 15-25%. Teacher salaries will rise by 25%, while state employees, military personnel, and students will see increases of 20%. Minimum wage is raised to 1300 somoni. Funding for these increases will come from the state budget.

item.title: Chinese President Xi Jinping Proposes Four Initiatives for Regional Development at SCO Summit
item.description: At the 26th SCO Summit in Bishkek, Chinese President Xi Jinping delivered a keynote address, proposing four initiatives for regional development and enhanced cooperation. He emphasized prioritizing development, security, people-centered approaches, and improved governance, calling for upholding the 'Shanghai Spirit' and building a community with a shared future.

item.title: Uzbek President Addresses Shanghai Cooperation Organisation Summit
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev expressed gratitude for the warm welcome and excellent organization of the SCO summit in Kyrgyzstan. He congratulated the Kyrgyz people on their 35th anniversary of state sovereignty and noted Kyrgyzstan's development and international standing. Mirziyoyev also acknowledged Kazakhstan's progress and supported the SCO's agenda and decisions, highlighting its 25th anniversary and role in regional stability.

item.title: Uzbek President Reviews 25 Years of Shanghai Cooperation Organisation
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev participated in the jubilee 25th anniversary meeting of the SCO Heads of State Council in Bishkek. The meeting, chaired by Kyrgyzstan's President Sadyr Japarov, discussed achievements, future tasks for stability, cooperation, and development. Leaders also exchanged views on current international and regional issues. Participants congratulated Uzbekistan on its Independence Day and praised its domestic reforms and foreign policy.

item.title: Iran's central bank assures sufficient foreign currency reserves despite US sanctions
item.description: Iran's central bank governor stated the country has sufficient foreign currency reserves, despite US sanctions. The bank is prepared to allocate up to $2 billion to stabilize the currency market. While acknowledging economic difficulties, the governor emphasized the financial system has not collapsed.

item.title: Uzbekistan Favors Open, Mutually Beneficial Cooperation in Eurasian Space, Says President Mirziyoyev
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev stated at the SCO Plus meeting that Uzbekistan favors developing open and mutually beneficial cooperation in the Eurasian space. He emphasized that greater commonality between countries and regions strengthens stability and mutual trust. The president participated and delivered a speech at the meeting format.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Ambassador Compares Nation's Development to China's Modernization
item.description: China's Ambassador to Uzbekistan, Yu Jun, drew parallels between China's modernization under the Communist Party and Uzbekistan's "New Uzbekistan" initiative. He highlighted China's focus on modernization, common prosperity, balanced development, human-nature harmony, and peaceful development. Uzbekistan is pursuing economic growth, legal reforms, and improved living standards.

item.title: Russian forces launch massive strike on Kyiv and other Ukrainian regions, causing civilian casualties
item.description: Russian forces conducted a massive overnight strike on Kyiv, the Kyiv region, and other Ukrainian oblasts, including Odesa and Kharkiv. Dozens were killed and injured, with damage to residential buildings, infrastructure, and enterprises. Railway infrastructure was a key target, with ballistic missiles destroying facilities and killing seven railway workers.

item.title: Tashkent Opens First Center for Contemporary Art in Uzbekistan
item.description: Tashkent will launch "CCA Tashkent" on September 6, the first permanent institution dedicated to contemporary art in Uzbekistan. Housed in a restored 1912 power station, the center will feature exhibition, educational, and research functions, aiming to connect local artists with the international art community.

item.title: Uzbek Craftsmanship Showcased at Venice Exhibition
item.description: Uzbekistan is presenting its craft heritage at the "Homo Faber-2026: An Island of Light" exhibition in Venice, opening September 1. The display features works by four artisans, including large ceramic "Moonjars" and knives from the Kamolov blacksmith dynasty, demonstrating traditional crafts in a contemporary context.
